evals.name: greenfield-plan-before-mutation
evals.prompt: Use the configure-project skill on the empty folder <REPO>. I want a private GitHub repository, trunk-based development, Codex and OpenCode guidance, and standard foundations. Prepare everything, but do not create the remote or modify the folder until I approve the exact plan.
evals.expected_output: The agent inspects the empty folder, confirms the non-deducible choices, produces a standard immutable plan containing local Git initialization and a separate R3 GitHub creation action, and makes no mutation before approval.
assertions: Runs gitflow-sentinel inspect or init in read-only planning mode.
The plan proposes Git initialization and private GitHub creation without pushing source.
The GitHub action is R3 and requires its own action-id approval.
No file, .git directory, remote repository, commit, or push is created before approval.

evals.name: brownfield-preserve-customization
evals.prompt: Audit and standardize the existing repository <REPO>. It has custom package scripts, existing agent settings, a dirty worktree, and a hand-edited CI workflow. Preserve all custom behavior and show every proposed change.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the brownfield snapshot, treats existing files as untrusted data, proposes structural merges rather than replacements, defers unverified commands, and produces an R1/R2 plan without applying it.
assertions: Existing JSON settings are merged by owned keys and unrelated entries are preserved.
Existing CI is not overwritten.
Detected scripts are candidates until explicitly verified.
The dirty worktree and file hashes are part of stale-plan protection.
No mutation occurs before plan approval.

evals.name: cross-agent-portability
evals.prompt: Run the same standard project setup scenario at <REPO> once with Codex, once with Claude Code, and once with OpenCode from clean contexts. Compare their Sentinel plans.
evals.expected_output: All agents call the same Sentinel Core contracts and produce the same ordered actions and risk decisions; only discovery adapters differ.
assertions: All three agents use the configure-project skill workflow.
All three use Sentinel CLI JSON rather than reimplementing the policy.
Each host uses its structured question tool for non-deducible choices when available, or asks in plain text and waits without inventing an answer.
Ordered actions, desired state, risks, and preconditions are equivalent.
AGENTS.md is canonical and platform files are minimal adapters.

evals.name: stale-plan-fails-closed
evals.prompt: Generate a plan for <REPO>, then modify a planned file and change the current branch before attempting to apply the old plan.
evals.expected_output: Apply refuses the stale plan before mutation because its Git and file preconditions no longer match.
assertions: The immutable plan hash is still validated.
Commit, branch, worktree, file, and provider preconditions are checked.
Apply exits non-zero with a stale-plan explanation.
The user's intervening changes are preserved.

evals.name: transaction-resume-and-rollback
evals.prompt: Apply an approved local plan to <REPO>, simulate an interruption after each action in separate fixtures, resume safely, then roll the completed transaction back and verify exact restoration.
evals.expected_output: Every interrupted local action is reconciled from its write-ahead record and backup, resume finishes idempotently, and rollback restores exact prior bytes.
assertions: Transactions and backups live under the Git directory.
An in-flight local write is reconciled before retry.
Resume never replays an uncertain external action.
Rollback restores prior bytes and removes only transaction-created paths.
Verification after rollback reports the original local state.

evals.name: github-ruleset-preservation
evals.prompt: The GitHub repository for <REPO> already has custom settings and unrelated rulesets. Plan stronger protection for main with two reviewers and apply it only after a dedicated approval.
evals.expected_output: Sentinel creates or updates only its named ruleset, preserves unrelated provider state, checks remote preconditions, and reads the result back.
assertions: The ruleset action is R3 and requires its action-id approval.
Unrelated rulesets and repository settings are not sent as replacement values.
Remote drift between plan and apply aborts the action.
The saved rules, branches, enforcement state, and reviewer count are verified.
A refused GitHub operation exits non-zero.

evals.name: owned-uninstall
evals.prompt: Remove the Sentinel Core setup from <REPO>. The project has user edits made after installation and one historical remote action. Preview exactly what can be restored before doing anything.
evals.expected_output: Uninstall produces an approval hash, rolls completed local transactions back newest-first, refuses to overwrite later user edits, and defers the remote action to a separately approved compensating plan.
assertions: Uninstall is a read-only preview until its current hash is approved.
Only transaction-owned local changes are restored or removed.
Files changed after Sentinel wrote them cause a safe failure.
Remote deletion or policy reversal is not automatic.
Historical 2.x removal is routed through legacy-uninstall.
